source_text:
Ὁ δέ,

ἐπείπερ ἦν πονηρὸς καὶ βάσκανος, ἐπεβούλευσε τῷ γένει, ἀντετάττετο τῇ βουλήσει
τοῦ δημιουργοῦ, κατεκόμισε πανούργως εἰς παρακοήν, εἰδὼς ὅτι πεσεῖται δι' αὐτῆς
εἰς θάνατον.
orientation: The homilist has just stated God's will that humanity be incorruptible, and now turns to the unnamed adversary who opposed that will.
pass_a_gloss: The [one] however, since he was wicked and envious, plotted against the race, was opposing the will of the creator, brought down cunningly into disobedience, knowing that he will fall through it into death.

choices.why: The brief identifies this as the unnamed adversary; the bare pronoun is kept as a pronoun to preserve the source's anonymity and contrast with God.
The dative τῷ γένει is the target of the plotting; 'the race' keeps the collective noun for humanity from the brief.
The imperfect tense shows ongoing, repeated opposition to the Creator's will, not a single act.
The verb means to bring down or carry down; the object is the race, and the direction is into disobedience, so 'brought it down' preserves the downward motion.
The adverb describes the manner of the adversary's action as crafty and sly, matching the brief's description of his cunning plot.

choices.term: εἰδὼς ὅτι πεσεῖται δι' αὐτῆς εἰς θάνατον
choices.english: knowing that it would fall through it into death
choices.why: The participle εἰδὼς is causal or attendant circumstance; the future πεσεῖται is retained as future from the adversary's perspective; δι' αὐτῆς refers back to disobedience.
rejected: since he knew that it would fall by it into death
knowing that through it it would fall into death

pass_b_english: But he, since he was wicked and envious, plotted against the race, was opposing the will of the Creator, and cunningly brought it down into disobedience, knowing that through it it would fall into death.
